text:
Dear Mr Gisler,

the first thing I did, that same evening and without waiting to speak to CSS, was call my bank and have my credit card blocked. It was in the saddlebag, and I knew from a friend, Peter Foster, that stolen cards are often used within the hour. I simply couldn't afford to wait until your office opened the next morning.

I'm sorry to say I can't give you any receipts. I don't have a single one for the things that were taken, and I've no way of getting copies: the bike came from a private sale, the saddlebag was a present and the shop where I bought the helmet has since closed.

Apart from that, there's nothing more for me to do to keep the loss down. The card was blocked, the police have the frame number, and I've checked the online marketplaces. That's all done.

What was stolen was mainly my bike, a men's racing bike with a carbon frame, a proper road bike with gears and pedals, nothing electric. I'd saved for a long time for it. With the saddlebag and the helmet it comes to CHF 5,150.

The theft happened at home, at Gartenstrasse 118 in Winterthur, on Tuesday 3 March 2026, some time between 7 and 10 in the evening.

Please let me know how you'd like to proceed.

Best wishes,
Henry Hughes
